plot.description: Plots a series of data on the chart.

Plots up and down arrows on the chart. Up arrow is drawn at every indicator positive value, down arrow is drawn at every negative value.  
If indicator returns [na](#var_na) then no arrow is drawn.  
Arrows has different height, the more absolute indicator value the longer arrow is drawn.

Creates alert condition, that is available in Create Alert dialog. Please note, that [alertcondition](#fun_alertcondition) does NOT create an alert, it just gives you more options in Create Alert dialog.  
Also, [alertcondition](#fun_alertcondition) effect is invisible on chart.

input.name: input
input.description: Adds an input to the Inputs tab of your script\`s Settings, which allows you to provide configuration options to script users. This function automatically detects the type of the argument used for 'defval' and uses the corresponding input widget.
input.syntaxExample: input(defval, title, tooltip, inline, group, display) → input bool|color|int|string|float

input.bool.name: input.bool
input.bool.description: Adds an input to the Inputs tab of your script\`s Settings, which allows you to provide configuration options to script users. This function adds a checkmark to the script\`s inputs.
input.bool.syntaxExample: input.bool(defval, title, tooltip, inline, group, confirm, display, active) → input bool

input.int.name: input.int
input.int.description: Adds an input to the Inputs tab of your script\`s Settings, which allows you to provide configuration options to script users. This function adds a field for an integer input to the script\`s inputs.
input.int.syntaxExample:
input.int(defval, title, minval, maxval, step, tooltip, inline, group, confirm, display) → input int
input.int(defval, title, options, tooltip, inline, group, confirm, display) → input int

input.float.name: input.float
input.float.description: Adds an input to the Inputs tab of your script\`s Settings, which allows you to provide configuration options to script users. This function adds a field for a float input to the script\`s inputs.
input.float.syntaxExample:
input.float(defval, title, minval, maxval, step, tooltip, inline, group, confirm, display) → input float
input.float(defval, title, options, tooltip, inline, group, confirm, display) → input float

input.string.name: input.string
input.string.description: Adds an input to the Inputs tab of your script\`s Settings, which allows you to provide configuration options to script users. This function adds a field for a string input to the script\`s inputs.
input.string.syntaxExample: input.string(defval, title, options, tooltip, inline, group, confirm, display, active) → input string

input.text_area.name: input.text_area
input.text_area.description: Adds an input to the Inputs tab of your script\`s Settings, which allows you to provide configuration options to script users. This function adds a field for a multiline text input.
input.text_area.syntaxExample: input.text_area(defval, title, tooltip, group, confirm, display, active) → input string

input.symbol.name: input.symbol
input.symbol.description: Adds an input to the Inputs tab of your script\`s Settings, which allows you to provide configuration options to script users. This function adds a field that allows the user to select a specific symbol using the symbol search and returns that symbol, paired with its exchange prefix, as a string.
input.symbol.syntaxExample: input.symbol(defval, title, tooltip, inline, group, confirm, display, active) → input string

input.timeframe.name: input.timeframe
input.timeframe.description: Adds an input to the Inputs tab of your script\`s Settings, which allows you to provide configuration options to script users. This function adds a dropdown that allows the user to select a specific timeframe via the timeframe selector and returns it as a string. The selector includes the custom timeframes a user may have added using the chart\`s Timeframe dropdown.
input.timeframe.syntaxExample: input.timeframe(defval, title, options, tooltip, inline, group, confirm, display, active) → input string

input.session.name: input.session
input.session.description: Adds an input to the Inputs tab of your script\`s Settings, which allows you to provide configuration options to script users. This function adds two dropdowns that allow the user to specify the beginning and the end of a session using the session selector and returns the result as a string.
input.session.syntaxExample: input.session(defval, title, options, tooltip, inline, group, confirm, display, active) → input string

input.source.name: input.source
input.source.description:
Adds an input to the Inputs tab of your script\`s Settings, which allows you to provide configuration options to script users.  
This function adds a dropdown that allows the user to select a source for the calculation, e.g. [close](#var_close), [hl2](#var_hl2), etc.  
The user can also select an output from another indicator on their chart as the source.
input.source.syntaxExample: input.source(defval, title, tooltip, inline, group, display, active, confirm) → series float

input.color.name: input.color
input.color.description: Adds an input to the Inputs tab of your script\`s Settings, which allows you to provide configuration options to script users. This function adds a color picker that allows the user to select a color and transparency, either from a palette or a hex value.
input.color.syntaxExample: input.color(defval, title, tooltip, inline, group, confirm, display, active) → input color

input.time.name: input.time
input.time.description:
Adds a time input to the script\`s "Settings/Inputs" tab. This function adds two input widgets on the same line: one for the date and one for the time.  
The function returns a date/time value in UNIX format.  
Using `confirm = true` activates the interactive input mode where a point in time is selected by clicking on the chart.
input.time.syntaxExample: input.time(defval, title, tooltip, inline, group, confirm, display, active) → input int

input.price.name: input.price
input.price.description: Adds a price input to the script\`s "Settings/Inputs" tab. Using `confirm = true` activates the interactive input mode where a price is selected by clicking on the chart.
input.price.syntaxExample: input.price(defval, title, tooltip, inline, group, confirm, display, active) → input float

math.min.name: math.min

returns: The smallest of multiple given values.

math.min.description: Returns the smallest of multiple values.

math.max.name: math.max

returns: The greatest of multiple given values.

math.max.description: Returns the greatest of multiple values.

math.abs.name: math.abs
math.abs.description: Absolute value of `number` is `number` if `number` >= 0, or if `number` is < 0 `number` is `(-2 * number)`

math.log.name: math.log
math.log.description: Natural logarithm of any `number` > 0 is the unique y such that e^y = `number`.

math.log10.name: math.log10
math.log10.description:
The common (or base 10) logarithm of `number` is the power to which 10 must be raised to obtain the `number`.  
10^y = `number`.

math.sqrt.name: math.sqrt
math.sqrt.description: Square root of any `number` >= 0 is the unique y >= 0 such that y^2 = `number`.

math.sign.name: math.sign
math.sign.description: Sign (signum) of `number` is zero if `number` is zero, 1.0 if `number` is greater than zero, -1.0 if `number` is less than zero.

math.exp.name: math.exp

returns: A value representing e raised to the power of `number`.

math.exp.description: The exp function of `number` is e raised to the power of `number`, where e is Euler\`s number.

math.sin.name: math.sin

returns: The trigonometric sine of an angle.

math.sin.description: The sin function returns the trigonometric sine of an angle.

math.cos.name: math.cos

returns: The trigonometric cosine of an angle.

math.cos.description: The cos function returns the trigonometric cosine of an angle.

math.tan.name: math.tan

returns: The trigonometric tangent of an angle.

math.tan.description: The tan function returns the trigonometric tangent of an angle.

math.asin.name: math.asin

returns: The arcsine of a value; the returned angle is in the range [-Pi/2
or [na](#var_na) if y is outside of range [-1

math.asin.description: The asin function returns the arcsine (in radians) of number such that sin(asin(y)) = y for y in range [-1, 1].

math.acos.name: math.acos

returns: The arc cosine of a value; the returned angle is in the range [0
or [na](#var_na) if y is outside of range [-1

math.acos.description: The acos function returns the arccosine (in radians) of number such that cos(acos(y)) = y for y in range [-1, 1].

math.atan.name: math.atan

returns: The arc tangent of a value; the returned angle is in the range [-Pi/2

math.atan.description: The atan function returns the arctangent (in radians) of number such that tan(atan(y)) = y for any y.

math.ceil.name: math.ceil

returns: The smallest integer greater than or equal to the given number.

math.ceil.description: The ceil function returns the smallest (closest to negative infinity) integer that is greater than or equal to the argument.

math.floor.name: math.floor

returns: The largest integer less than or equal to the given number.

math.floor.description: The floor function returns the largest (closest to positive infinity) integer that is less than or equal to the argument.

math.round.name: math.round

returns: The value of `number` rounded to the nearest integer

math.round.description:
Returns the value of `number` rounded to the nearest integer, with ties rounding up.  
If the `precision` parameter is used, returns a float value rounded to that amount of decimal places.

math.round_to_mintick.name: math.round_to_mintick
math.round_to_mintick.description: Returns the value rounded to the symbol\`s mintick, i.e. the nearest value that can be divided by [syminfo.mintick](#var_syminfo.mintick), without the remainder, with ties rounding up.

ta.median.name: ta.median
ta.median.description: Returns the median of the series.

ta.max.name: ta.max
ta.max.description: Returns the all-time high value of `source` from the beginning of the chart up to the current bar.

ta.min.name: ta.min
ta.min.description: Returns the all-time low value of `source` from the beginning of the chart up to the current bar.

ta.mode.name: ta.mode

returns: The most frequently occurring value from the `source`. If none exists

ta.mode.description:
Returns the [mode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mode_(statistics)) of the series.  
If there are several values with the same frequency, it returns the smallest value.

ta.range.name: ta.range

returns: The difference between the min and max values in the series.

ta.range.description: Returns the difference between the min and max values in a series.

math.todegrees.name: math.todegrees
math.todegrees.description: Returns an approximately equivalent angle in degrees from an angle measured in radians.

math.toradians.name: math.toradians
math.toradians.description: Returns an approximately equivalent angle in radians from an angle measured in degrees.

math.random.name: math.random
math.random.description: Returns a pseudo-random value. The function will generate a different sequence of values for each script execution. Using the same value for the optional seed argument will produce a repeatable sequence.

math.sum.name: math.sum
math.sum.description: The sum function returns the sliding sum of last y values of x.

ta.sma.name: ta.sma

returns: Simple moving average of `source` for `length` bars back.

ta.sma.description: The sma function returns the moving average, that is the sum of last y values of x, divided by y.

ta.hma.name: ta.hma

returns: Hull moving average of 'source' for 'length' bars back.

ta.hma.description: The hma function returns the Hull Moving Average.

ta.ema.name: ta.ema

returns: Exponential moving average of `source` with alpha = 2 / (length + 1).

ta.ema.description: The ema function returns the exponentially weighted moving average. In ema weighting factors decrease exponentially. It calculates by using a formula: EMA = alpha * source + (1 - alpha) * EMA[1], where alpha = 2 / (length + 1).

ta.wma.name: ta.wma

returns: Weighted moving average of `source` for `length` bars back.

ta.wma.description:
The wma function returns weighted moving average of `source` for `length` bars back.  
In wma weighting factors decrease in arithmetical progression.

ta.vwma.name: ta.vwma

returns: Volume-weighted moving average of `source` for `length` bars back.

ta.vwma.description:
The vwma function returns volume-weighted moving average of `source` for `length` bars back.  
It is the same as: sma(source * volume, length) / sma(volume, length).

ta.supertrend.name: ta.supertrend

returns: [Tuple](https://www.tradingview.com/pine-script-docs/en/v6/language/Type_system.html#tuples) of two supertrend series: supertrend line and direction of trend. Possible values are 1 (down direction) and -1 (up direction).

ta.supertrend.description: The Supertrend Indicator. The Supertrend is a trend following indicator.

ta.macd.name: ta.macd

returns: [Tuple](https://www.tradingview.com/pine-script-docs/en/v6/language/Type_system.html#tuples) of three MACD series: MACD line

ta.macd.description: MACD (moving average convergence/divergence). It is supposed to reveal changes in the strength, direction, momentum, and duration of a trend in a stock\`s price.
ta.macd.syntaxExample: ta.macd(source, fastlen, slowlen, siglen) → [series float, series float, series float]

ta.lowest.name: ta.lowest
ta.lowest.description: Lowest value for a given number of bars back.
ta.lowest.syntaxExample:
ta.lowest(source, length) → series float
ta.lowest(length) → series float

ta.highest.name: ta.highest
ta.highest.description: Highest value for a given number of bars back.

ta.lowestbars.name: ta.lowestbars
ta.lowestbars.description: Lowest value offset for a given number of bars back.
ta.lowestbars.syntaxExample:
ta.lowestbars(source, length) → series int
ta.lowestbars(length) → series int

ta.highestbars.name: ta.highestbars
ta.highestbars.description: Highest value offset for a given number of bars back.
ta.highestbars.syntaxExample:
ta.highestbars(source, length) → series int
ta.highestbars(length) → series int

ta.barssince.name: ta.barssince

returns: Number of bars since condition was true.

ta.barssince.description: Counts the number of bars since the last time the condition was true.

ta.valuewhen.name: ta.valuewhen
ta.valuewhen.description: Returns the value of the `source` series on the bar where the `condition` was true on the nth most recent occurrence.

ta.falling.name: ta.falling

returns: true if current `source` value is less than any previous `source` value for `length` bars back

ta.falling.description: Test if the `source` series is now falling for `length` bars long.

ta.rising.name: ta.rising

returns: true if current `source` is greater than any previous `source` for `length` bars back

ta.rising.description: Test if the `source` series is now rising for `length` bars long.

ta.roc.name: ta.roc

returns: The rate of change of `source` for `length` bars back.

ta.roc.description:
Calculates the percentage of change (rate of change) between the current value of `source` and its value `length` bars ago.
It is calculated by the formula: 100 * change(src, length) / src[length].

ta.cci.name: ta.cci

returns: Commodity channel index of source for length bars back.

ta.cci.description: The CCI (commodity channel index) is calculated as the difference between the typical price of a commodity and its simple moving average, divided by the mean absolute deviation of the typical price. The index is scaled by an inverse factor of 0.015 to provide more readable numbers.

ta.variance.name: ta.variance
ta.variance.description: Variance is the expectation of the squared deviation of a series from its mean ([ta.sma](#fun_ta.sma)), and it informally measures how far a set of numbers are spread out from their mean.

ta.dev.name: ta.dev
ta.dev.description: Measure of difference between the series and it\`s [ta.sma](#fun_ta.sma)

ta.percentrank.name: ta.percentrank

returns: Percent rank of `source` for `length` bars back.

ta.percentrank.description: Percent rank is the percents of how many previous values was less than or equal to the current value of given series.

ta.rma.name: ta.rma

returns: Exponential moving average of `source` with alpha = 1 / `length`.

ta.rma.description: Moving average used in RSI. It is the exponentially weighted moving average with alpha = 1 / length.

ta.rsi.name: ta.rsi
ta.rsi.description: Relative strength index. It is calculated using the `ta.rma()` of upward and downward changes of `source` over the last `length` bars.

timeframe.from_seconds.name: timeframe.from_seconds

returns: A timeframe string compliant with [timeframe string specifications](https://www.tradingview.com/pine-script-docs/en/v6/concepts/Timeframes.html#timeframe-string-specifications).

timeframe.from_seconds.description:
Converts a number of seconds into a valid timeframe string.  
1m = 60, 5m = 300, 15m = 900, 30m = 1800, 1h = 3600, 4h = 14400, 1D = 86400

timeframe.in_seconds.name: timeframe.in_seconds

returns: An int representation of the number of seconds in one bar of a `timeframe`.

timeframe.in_seconds.description: Converts the timeframe passed to the `timeframe` argument into seconds.

ta.dmi.name: ta.dmi

returns: [Tuple](https://www.tradingview.com/pine-script-docs/en/v6/language/Type_system.html#tuples) of three DMI series: Positive Directional Movement (+DI)
Negative Directional Movement (-DI) and Average Directional Movement Index (ADX).

ta.dmi.description: The dmi function returns the directional movement index.
ta.dmi.syntaxExample: ta.dmi(diLength, adxSmoothing) → [series float, series float, series float]

ta.correlation.name: ta.correlation
ta.correlation.description: Correlation coefficient. Describes the degree to which two series tend to deviate from their [ta.sma](#fun_ta.sma) values.

ta.tsi.name: ta.tsi

returns: True strength index. A value in range [-1

ta.tsi.description: True strength index. It uses moving averages of the underlying momentum of a financial instrument.

ta.linreg.name: ta.linreg
ta.linreg.description:
Linear regression curve. A line that best fits the prices specified over a user-defined time period.  
It is calculated using the least squares method.  
The result of this function is calculated using the formula: linreg = intercept + slope * (length - 1 - offset), where intercept and slope are the values calculated with the least squares method on `source` series.

ta.stoch.name: ta.stoch
ta.stoch.description: Stochastic. It is calculated by a formula: 100 * (close - lowest(low, length)) / (highest(high, length) - lowest(low, length)).
ta.stoch.syntaxExample: ta.stoch(source, high, low, length) → series float

ta.atr.name: ta.atr
ta.atr.description: Function atr (average true range) returns the RMA of true range. True range is max(high - low, abs(high - close[1]), abs(low - close[1])).

fixnan.name: fixnan
fixnan.description: For a given series replaces NaN values with previous nearest non-NaN value.

ta.cum.name: ta.cum
ta.cum.description: Cumulative (total) sum of `source`. In other words it\`s a sum of all elements of `source`.

ta.change.name: ta.change

returns: The difference between the values when they are numerical. When a 'bool' source is used
returns `true` when the current source is different from the previous source.

ta.change.description: Compares the current `source` value to its value `length` bars ago and returns the difference.

ta.mom.name: ta.mom

returns: Momentum of `source` price and `source` price `length` bars ago.

ta.mom.description: Momentum of `source` price and `source` price `length` bars ago. This is simply a difference: source - source[length].

ta.pivot_point_levels.name: ta.pivot_point_levels

strategy.entry.name: strategy.entry
strategy.entry.description:
It is a command to enter market position. If an order with the same ID is already pending, it is possible to modify the order.  
If there is no order with the specified ID, a new order is placed.  
To deactivate an entry order, the command [strategy.cancel](#fun_strategy.cancel) or [strategy.cancel_all](#fun_strategy.cancel_all) should be used.  
In comparison to the function [strategy.order](#fun_strategy.order), the function [strategy.entry](#fun_strategy.entry) is affected by pyramiding and it can reverse market position correctly.  
If both 'limit' and 'stop' parameters are 'NaN', the order type is market order.
strategy.entry.syntaxExample: strategy.entry(id, direction, qty, limit, stop, oca_name, oca_type, comment, alert_message, disable_alert) → void

strategy.order.name: strategy.order
strategy.order.description:
It is a command to place order. If an order with the same ID is already pending, it is possible to modify the order.  
If there is no order with the specified ID, a new order is placed.  
To deactivate order, the command [strategy.cancel](#fun_strategy.cancel) or [strategy.cancel_all](#fun_strategy.cancel_all) should be used.  
In comparison to the function [strategy.entry](#fun_strategy.entry), the function [strategy.order](#fun_strategy.order) is not affected by pyramiding.  
If both 'limit' and 'stop' parameters are 'NaN', the order type is market order.
strategy.order.syntaxExample: strategy.order(id, direction, qty, limit, stop, oca_name, oca_type, comment, alert_message, disable_alert) → void

strategy.exit.name: strategy.exit
strategy.exit.description:
It is a command to exit either a specific entry, or whole market position. If an order with the same ID is already pending, it is possible to modify the order.  
If an entry order was not filled, but an exit order is generated, the exit order will wait till entry order is filled and then the exit order is placed.  
To deactivate an exit order, the command [strategy.cancel](#fun_strategy.cancel) or [strategy.cancel_all](#fun_strategy.cancel_all) should be used.  
If the function [strategy.exit](#fun_strategy.exit) is called once, it exits a position only once.  
If you want to exit multiple times, the command [strategy.exit](#fun_strategy.exit) should be called multiple times.  
If you use a stop loss and a trailing stop, their order type is 'stop', so only one of them is placed (the one that is supposed to be filled first).  
If all the following parameters 'profit', 'limit', 'loss', 'stop', 'trail_points', 'trail_offset' are 'NaN', the command will fail.  
To use market order to exit, the command [strategy.close](#fun_strategy.close) or [strategy.close_all](#fun_strategy.close_all) should be used.
strategy.exit.syntaxExample: strategy.exit(id, from_entry, qty, qty_percent, profit, limit, loss, stop, trail_price, trail_points, trail_offset, oca_name, comment, comment_profit, comment_loss, comment_trailing, alert_message, alert_profit, alert_loss, alert_trailing, disable_alert) → void

max_bars_back.name: max_bars_back
max_bars_back.description:
Function sets the maximum number of bars that is available for historical reference of a given built-in or user variable.  
When operator '[]' is applied to a variable - it is a reference to a historical value of that variable.

If an argument of an operator '[]' is a compile time constant value (e.g. 'v[10]', 'close[500]') then there is no need to use 'max_bars_back' function for that variable.  
Pine Script™ compiler will use that constant value as history buffer size.

If an argument of an operator '[]' is a value, calculated at runtime (e.g. 'v[i]' where 'i' - is a series variable) then Pine Script™ attempts to autodetect the history buffer size at runtime.  
Sometimes it fails and the script crashes at runtime because it eventually refers to historical values that are out of the buffer.  
In that case you should use 'max_bars_back' to fix that problem manually.

simple.name: simple
simple.description:
**simple** is a keyword that can be used in a library\`s exported functions to specify the type form required for a function\`s arguments.  
By default, all arguments of exported functions are automatically converted into the "series" type form.  
In some cases, this would make arguments unusable with those of built-in functions that do not support the "series" form.  
For these cases, the `simple` keyword can be used instead.

series.name: series
series.description:
**series** is a keyword that can be used in a library\`s exported functions to specify the type form required for a function\`s arguments.  
Explicit use of the `series` keyword is usually unnecessary because all arguments of exported functions are automatically converted to the "series" form by default.

footprint.description: Volume footprint data for a bar. Contains price-level volume information.

volume_row.name: volume_row
volume_row.description: A price-level row in a footprint. Contains volume data at a specific price level.

const.name: const
const.description:
**const** is a type qualifier for values known at compile time, before the script is executed. A "const" value never changes for the life of a script.  
Literal values (e.g., `1`, `"AAPL"`) and expressions composed entirely of other "const" values automatically qualify as "const".

matrix.name: matrix

Matrix objects are always of "series" form.

map.name: map
map.description:
Keyword used to explicitly declare the "map" type of a variable or a parameter. Map objects (or IDs) can be created with the `map.new<type,type>()` function.  
Map objects are always of "series" form.

session.isfirstbar.name: session.isfirstbar
session.isfirstbar.description:
Returns [true](#op_true) if the current bar is the first bar of the day\`s session, `false` otherwise.  
If extended session information is used, only returns [true](#op_true) on the first bar of the pre-market bars.

session.islastbar.name: session.islastbar
session.islastbar.description:
Returns [true](#op_true) if the current bar is the last bar of the day\`s session, `false` otherwise.  
If extended session information is used, only returns [true](#op_true) on the last bar of the post-market bars.

session.isfirstbar_regular.name: session.isfirstbar_regular
session.isfirstbar_regular.description:
Returns [true](#op_true) on the first regular session bar of the day, `false` otherwise.  
The result is the same whether extended session information is used or not.

session.islastbar_regular.name: session.islastbar_regular
session.islastbar_regular.description:
Returns [true](#op_true) on the last regular session bar of the day, `false` otherwise.  
The result is the same whether extended session information is used or not.

bar_index.name: bar_index
bar_index.description: Current bar index. Numbering is zero-based, index of the first bar is 0.

last_bar_index.name: last_bar_index
last_bar_index.description: Bar index of the last chart bar. Bar indices begin at zero on the first bar.

last_bar_time.name: last_bar_time
last_bar_time.description: Time in UNIX format of the last chart bar. It is the number of milliseconds that have elapsed since 00:00:00 UTC, 1 January 1970.

close.name: close
close.description: Close price of the current bar when it has closed, or last traded price of a yet incomplete, realtime bar.

hlc3.name: hlc3
hlc3.description: Is a shortcut for (high + low + close)/3

hlcc4.name: hlcc4
hlcc4.description: Is a shortcut for (high + low + close + close)/4

ohlc4.name: ohlc4
ohlc4.description: Is a shortcut for (open + high + low + close)/4

ta.accdist.name: ta.accdist
description: Accumulation/distribution index.

syminfo.tickerid.name: syminfo.tickerid
syminfo.tickerid.description:
Returns the full form of the ticker ID representing a symbol, for use as an argument in functions with a `ticker` or `symbol` parameter.  
It always includes the prefix (exchange) and ticker separated by a colon ("NASDAQ:AAPL"), but it can also include other symbol data such as dividend adjustment, chart type, currency conversion, etc.

syminfo.minmove.name: syminfo.minmove
syminfo.minmove.description:
Returns a whole number used to calculate the smallest increment between a symbol\`s price movements ([syminfo.mintick](#var_syminfo.mintick)).  
It is the numerator in the [syminfo.mintick](#var_syminfo.mintick) formula: '[syminfo.minmove](#var_syminfo.minmove) / [syminfo.pricescale](#var_syminfo.pricescale) = [syminfo.mintick](#var_syminfo.mintick)'.

syminfo.pricescale.name: syminfo.pricescale
syminfo.pricescale.description:
Returns a whole number used to calculate the smallest increment between a symbol\`s price movements ([syminfo.mintick](#var_syminfo.mintick)).  
It is the denominator in the [syminfo.mintick](#var_syminfo.mintick) formula: '[syminfo.minmove](#var_syminfo.minmove) / [syminfo.pricescale](#var_syminfo.pricescale) = [syminfo.mintick](#var_syminfo.mintick)'.

timeframe.period.name: timeframe.period
description: A string representation of the chart\`s timeframe. The returned string\`s format is "[<quantity>][<units>]", where <quantity> and <units> are in some cases absent. <quantity> is the number of units, but it is absent if that number is 1. <unit> is "S" for seconds, "D" for days, "W" for weeks, "M" for months, but it is absent for minutes. No <unit> exists for hours.
The variable will return: "10S" for 10 seconds, "60" for 60 minutes, "D" for one day, "2W" for two weeks, "3M" for one quarter.
Can be used as an argument with any function containing a `timeframe` parameter.

syminfo.root.name: syminfo.root
syminfo.root.description: Root for derivatives like futures contract. For other symbols returns the same value as [syminfo.ticker](#var_syminfo.ticker).

syminfo.mintick.name: syminfo.mintick
syminfo.mintick.description: Min tick value for the current symbol.

syminfo.pointvalue.name: syminfo.pointvalue
syminfo.pointvalue.description: Point value for the current symbol.

syminfo.session.name: syminfo.session
syminfo.session.description: Session type of the chart main series. Possible values are [session.regular](#const_session.regular), [session.extended](#const_session.extended).

syminfo.timezone.name: syminfo.timezone
syminfo.timezone.description: Timezone of the exchange of the chart main series. Possible values see in [timestamp](#fun_timestamp).

syminfo.currency.name: syminfo.currency
syminfo.currency.description: Currency for the current symbol. Returns currency code: 'USD', 'EUR', etc.

syminfo.basecurrency.name: syminfo.basecurrency
syminfo.basecurrency.description: Base currency for the symbol. For the symbol 'BTCUSD' returns 'BTC'.

syminfo.type.name: syminfo.type
syminfo.type.description: Type of the current symbol. Possible values are stock, futures, index, forex, crypto, fund, dr.

syminfo.sector.name: syminfo.sector
syminfo.sector.description:
Returns the sector of the symbol, or [na](#var_na) if the symbol has no sector.  
Example: "Electronic Technology", "Technology services", "Energy Minerals", "Consumer Durables", etc.  
These are the same values one can see in the chart\`s "Symbol info" window.

syminfo.industry.name: syminfo.industry
syminfo.industry.description:
Returns the industry of the symbol, or [na](#var_na) if the symbol has no industry.  
Example: "Internet Software/Services", "Packaged software", "Integrated Oil", "Motor Vehicles", etc.  
These are the same values one can see in the chart\`s "Symbol info" window.

syminfo.country.name: syminfo.country
syminfo.country.description:
Returns the two-letter code of the country where the symbol is traded, in the [ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2) format, or [na](#var_na) if the exchange is not directly tied to a specific country.  
For example, on "NASDAQ:AAPL" it will return "US", on "LSE:AAPL" it will return "GB", and on "BITSTAMP:BTCUSD it will return [na](#var_na).

syminfo.volumetype.name: syminfo.volumetype
syminfo.volumetype.description: Volume type of the current symbol. Possible values are: "base" for base currency, "quote" for quote currency, "tick" for the number of transactions, and "n/a" when there is no volume or its type is not specified.

timeframe.isdwm.name: timeframe.isdwm
timeframe.isdwm.description: Returns true if current resolution is a daily or weekly or monthly resolution, false otherwise.

timeframe.isintraday.name: timeframe.isintraday
timeframe.isintraday.description: Returns true if current resolution is an intraday (minutes or seconds) resolution, false otherwise.

timeframe.isdaily.name: timeframe.isdaily
timeframe.isdaily.description: Returns true if current resolution is a daily resolution, false otherwise.

timeframe.isweekly.name: timeframe.isweekly
timeframe.isweekly.description: Returns true if current resolution is a weekly resolution, false otherwise.

timeframe.ismonthly.name: timeframe.ismonthly
timeframe.ismonthly.description: Returns true if current resolution is a monthly resolution, false otherwise.

timeframe.isminutes.name: timeframe.isminutes
timeframe.isminutes.description: Returns true if current resolution is a minutes resolution, false otherwise.

timeframe.isseconds.name: timeframe.isseconds
timeframe.isseconds.description: Returns true if current resolution is a seconds resolution, false otherwise.

timenow.name: timenow
timenow.description: Current time in UNIX format. It is the number of milliseconds that have elapsed since 00:00:00 UTC, 1 January 1970.

time_tradingday.name: time_tradingday
time_tradingday.description: The beginning time of the trading day the current bar belongs to, in UNIX format (the number of milliseconds that have elapsed since 00:00:00 UTC, 1 January 1970).

strategy.position_size.name: strategy.position_size
strategy.position_size.description: Direction and size of the current market position. If the value is > 0, the market position is long. If the value is < 0, the market position is short. The absolute value is the number of contracts/shares/lots/units in trade (position size).

strategy.position_avg_price.name: strategy.position_avg_price
strategy.position_avg_price.description: Average entry price of current market position. If the market position is flat, 'NaN' is returned.

strategy.openprofit.name: strategy.openprofit
strategy.openprofit.description: Current unrealized profit or loss for all open positions.

strategy.netprofit.name: strategy.netprofit
strategy.netprofit.description: Total currency value of all completed trades.

strategy.position_entry_name.name: strategy.position_entry_name
strategy.position_entry_name.description: Name of the order that initially opened current market position.

strategy.grossprofit.name: strategy.grossprofit
strategy.grossprofit.description: Total currency value of all completed winning trades.

strategy.grossloss.name: strategy.grossloss
strategy.grossloss.description: Total currency value of all completed losing trades.

strategy.max_drawdown.name: strategy.max_drawdown
strategy.max_drawdown.description: Maximum equity drawdown value for the whole trading interval.

strategy.max_runup.name: strategy.max_runup
strategy.max_runup.description: Maximum equity run-up value for the whole trading interval.

strategy.max_contracts_held_all.name: strategy.max_contracts_held_all
strategy.max_contracts_held_all.description: Maximum number of contracts/shares/lots/units in one trade for the whole trading interval.

strategy.max_contracts_held_long.name: strategy.max_contracts_held_long
strategy.max_contracts_held_long.description: Maximum number of contracts/shares/lots/units in one long trade for the whole trading interval.

strategy.max_contracts_held_short.name: strategy.max_contracts_held_short
strategy.max_contracts_held_short.description: Maximum number of contracts/shares/lots/units in one short trade for the whole trading interval.

strategy.opentrades.name: strategy.opentrades
strategy.opentrades.description: Number of market position entries, which were not closed and remain opened. If there is no open market position, 0 is returned.

strategy.closedtrades.name: strategy.closedtrades
strategy.closedtrades.description: Number of trades which were closed for the whole trading interval. In Pine Script v6, trades exceeding the 9,000 limit are automatically trimmed from memory; use [strategy.closedtrades.first_index](#var_strategy.closedtrades.first_index) to find the first accessible closed trade.

strategy.wintrades.name: strategy.wintrades
strategy.wintrades.description: Number of profitable trades for the whole trading interval.

strategy.losstrades.name: strategy.losstrades
strategy.losstrades.description: Number of unprofitable trades for the whole trading interval.

strategy.eventrades.name: strategy.eventrades
strategy.eventrades.description: Number of breakeven trades for the whole trading interval.

strategy.initial_capital.name: strategy.initial_capital
strategy.initial_capital.description: The amount of initial capital set in the strategy properties.

strategy.account_currency.name: strategy.account_currency
strategy.account_currency.description: Returns the currency used to calculate results, which can be set in the strategy\`s properties.

strategy.margin_liquidation_price.name: strategy.margin_liquidation_price
strategy.margin_liquidation_price.description: When margin is used in a strategy, returns the price point where a simulated margin call will occur and liquidate enough of the position to meet the margin requirements.

strategy.grossloss_percent.name: strategy.grossloss_percent
strategy.grossloss_percent.description: The total value of all completed losing trades, expressed as a percentage of the initial capital.

strategy.max_runup_percent.name: strategy.max_runup_percent
strategy.max_runup_percent.description: The maximum equity run-up value for the whole trading interval, expressed as a percentage and calculated by formula: `Highest Value During Trade / (Entry Price x Quantity) * 100`.

strategy.netprofit_percent.name: strategy.netprofit_percent
strategy.netprofit_percent.description: The total value of all completed trades, expressed as a percentage of the initial capital.

strategy.openprofit_percent.name: strategy.openprofit_percent
strategy.openprofit_percent.description: The current unrealized profit or loss for all open positions, expressed as a percentage and calculated by formula: `openPL / realizedEquity * 100`.

strategy.grossprofit_percent.name: strategy.grossprofit_percent
strategy.grossprofit_percent.description: The total currency value of all completed winning trades, expressed as a percentage of the initial capital.

strategy.max_drawdown_percent.name: strategy.max_drawdown_percent
strategy.max_drawdown_percent.description: The maximum equity drawdown value for the whole trading interval, expressed as a percentage and calculated by formula: `Lowest Value During Trade / (Entry Price x Quantity) * 100`.

barstate.isfirst.name: barstate.isfirst
barstate.isfirst.description: Returns true if current bar is first bar in barset, false otherwise.

barstate.islast.name: barstate.islast
barstate.islast.description: Returns true if current bar is the last bar in barset, false otherwise. This condition is true for all real-time bars in barset.

barstate.ishistory.name: barstate.ishistory
barstate.ishistory.description: Returns true if current bar is a historical bar, false otherwise.

barstate.isrealtime.name: barstate.isrealtime
barstate.isrealtime.description: Returns true if current bar is a real-time bar, false otherwise.

barstate.isnew.name: barstate.isnew
barstate.isnew.description: Returns true if script is currently calculating on new bar, false otherwise. This variable is true when calculating on historical bars or on first update of a newly generated real-time bar.

barstate.isconfirmed.name: barstate.isconfirmed
barstate.isconfirmed.description: Returns true if the script is calculating the last (closing) update of the current bar. The next script calculation will be on the new bar data.

barstate.islastconfirmedhistory.name: barstate.islastconfirmedhistory
barstate.islastconfirmedhistory.description: Returns true if script is executing on the dataset\`s last bar when market is closed, or script is executing on the bar immediately preceding the real-time bar, if market is open. Returns false otherwise.

session.ismarket.name: session.ismarket
session.ismarket.description: Returns true if the current bar is a part of the regular trading hours (i.e. market hours), false otherwise

session.ispremarket.name: session.ispremarket
session.ispremarket.description: Returns true if the current bar is a part of the pre-market, false otherwise. On non-intraday charts always returns false.

session.ispostmarket.name: session.ispostmarket
session.ispostmarket.description: Returns true if the current bar is a part of the post-market, false otherwise. On non-intraday charts always returns false.

label.all.name: label.all
label.all.description: Returns an array filled with all the current labels drawn by the script.

line.all.name: line.all
line.all.description: Returns an array filled with all the current lines drawn by the script.

linefill.all.name: linefill.all
linefill.all.description: Returns an array filled with all the current linefill objects drawn by the script.

box.all.name: box.all
box.all.description: Returns an array filled with all the current boxes drawn by the script.

table.all.name: table.all
table.all.description: Returns an array filled with all the current tables drawn by the script.

polyline.all.name: polyline.all
polyline.all.description: Returns an array containing all current [polyline](#op_polyline) instances drawn by the script.

chart.bg_color.name: chart.bg_color
chart.bg_color.description: Returns the color of the chart\`s background from the "Chart settings/Appearance/Background" field. When a gradient is selected, the middle point of the gradient is returned.

chart.fg_color.name: chart.fg_color
chart.fg_color.description: Returns a color providing optimal contrast with [chart.bg_color](#var_chart.bg_color).

chart.left_visible_bar_time.name: chart.left_visible_bar_time
chart.left_visible_bar_time.description: The [time](#var_time) of the leftmost bar currently visible on the chart.

chart.right_visible_bar_time.name: chart.right_visible_bar_time
chart.right_visible_bar_time.description: The [time](#var_time) of the rightmost bar currently visible on the chart.

earnings.future_time.name: earnings.future_time
earnings.future_time.description: Returns a UNIX timestamp indicating the expected time of the next earnings report, or [na](#var_na) if this data isn't available.

earnings.future_period_end_time.name: earnings.future_period_end_time
earnings.future_period_end_time.description: Checks the data for the next earnings report and returns the UNIX timestamp of the day when the financial period covered by those earnings ends, or [na](#var_na) if this data isn't available.

earnings.future_eps.name: earnings.future_eps
earnings.future_eps.description: Returns the estimated Earnings per Share of the next earnings report in the currency of the instrument, or [na](#var_na) if this data isn't available.

earnings.future_revenue.name: earnings.future_revenue
earnings.future_revenue.description: Returns the estimated Revenue of the next earnings report in the currency of the instrument, or [na](#var_na) if this data isn't available.

syminfo.employees.name: syminfo.employees
syminfo.employees.description: The number of employees the company has.

syminfo.shareholders.name: syminfo.shareholders
syminfo.shareholders.description: The number of shareholders the company has.

syminfo.shares_outstanding_float.name: syminfo.shares_outstanding_float
syminfo.shares_outstanding_float.description: The total number of shares outstanding a company has available, excluding any of its restricted shares.

syminfo.shares_outstanding_total.name: syminfo.shares_outstanding_total
syminfo.shares_outstanding_total.description: The total number of shares outstanding a company has available, including restricted shares held by insiders, major shareholders, and employees.

syminfo.target_price_average.name: syminfo.target_price_average
syminfo.target_price_average.description: The average of the last yearly price targets for the symbol predicted by analysts.

syminfo.target_price_date.name: syminfo.target_price_date
syminfo.target_price_date.description: The starting date of the last price target prediction for the current symbol.

syminfo.target_price_estimates.name: syminfo.target_price_estimates
syminfo.target_price_estimates.description: The latest total number of price target predictions for the current symbol.

syminfo.target_price_high.name: syminfo.target_price_high
syminfo.target_price_high.description: The last highest yearly price target for the symbol predicted by analysts.

syminfo.target_price_low.name: syminfo.target_price_low
syminfo.target_price_low.description: The last lowest yearly price target for the symbol predicted by analysts.

syminfo.target_price_median.name: syminfo.target_price_median
syminfo.target_price_median.description: The median of the last yearly price targets for the symbol predicted by analysts.

syminfo.recommendations_buy.name: syminfo.recommendations_buy
syminfo.recommendations_buy.description: The number of analysts who gave the current symbol a "Buy" rating.

syminfo.recommendations_buy_strong.name: syminfo.recommendations_buy_strong
syminfo.recommendations_buy_strong.description: The number of analysts who gave the current symbol a "Strong Buy" rating.

syminfo.recommendations_date.name: syminfo.recommendations_date
syminfo.recommendations_date.description: The starting date of the last set of recommendations for the current symbol.

syminfo.recommendations_hold.name: syminfo.recommendations_hold
syminfo.recommendations_hold.description: The number of analysts who gave the current symbol a "Hold" rating.

syminfo.recommendations_total.name: syminfo.recommendations_total
syminfo.recommendations_total.description: The total number of recommendations for the current symbol.

syminfo.recommendations_sell.name: syminfo.recommendations_sell
syminfo.recommendations_sell.description: The number of analysts who gave the current symbol a "Sell" rating.

syminfo.recommendations_sell_strong.name: syminfo.recommendations_sell_strong
syminfo.recommendations_sell_strong.description: The number of analysts who gave the current symbol a "Strong Sell" rating.

bid.name: bid
bid.description: The highest active buyer price. Only available on the 1T (tick) timeframe.

ask.name: ask
ask.description: The lowest active seller price. Only available on the 1T (tick) timeframe.

strategy.closedtrades.first_index.name: strategy.closedtrades.first_index
strategy.closedtrades.first_index.description: The index of the earliest remaining closed trade in memory. In Pine Script v6, when a strategy exceeds 9,000 trades, the oldest trades are automatically trimmed. This variable returns the lowest valid trade_num that can be referenced by strategy.closedtrades.* functions.

syminfo.current_contract.name: syminfo.current_contract
syminfo.current_contract.description: Stores the ticker identifier of the underlying contract if the current symbol refers to a continuous futures dataset, and an empty string otherwise.

syminfo.expiration_date.name: syminfo.expiration_date

syminfo.isin.name: syminfo.isin

syminfo.mincontract.name: syminfo.mincontract

dividends.future_amount.name: dividends.future_amount
dividends.future_amount.description: Returns the payment amount of the upcoming dividend in the currency of the current instrument, or [na](#var_na) if this data isn't available.

dividends.future_ex_date.name: dividends.future_ex_date
dividends.future_ex_date.description: Returns the Ex-dividend date (Ex-date) of the current instrument's next dividend payment, or [na](#var_na) if this data isn't available. Ex-dividend date signifies when investors are no longer entitled to a payout from the most recent dividend. Only those who purchased shares before this day are entitled to the dividend payment.

dividends.future_pay_date.name: dividends.future_pay_date
dividends.future_pay_date.description: Returns the Payment date (Pay date) of the current instrument's next dividend payment, or [na](#var_na) if this data isn't available. Payment date signifies the day when eligible investors will receive the dividend payment.

strategy.avg_losing_trade.name: strategy.avg_losing_trade
strategy.avg_losing_trade.description: Returns the average amount of money lost per losing trade. Calculated as the sum of losses divided by the number of losing trades.

strategy.avg_losing_trade_percent.name: strategy.avg_losing_trade_percent
strategy.avg_losing_trade_percent.description: Returns the average percentage loss per losing trade. Calculated as the sum of loss percentages divided by the number of losing trades.

strategy.avg_trade.name: strategy.avg_trade

strategy.avg_trade_percent.name: strategy.avg_trade_percent

strategy.avg_winning_trade.name: strategy.avg_winning_trade

strategy.avg_winning_trade_percent.name: strategy.avg_winning_trade_percent
strategy.avg_winning_trade_percent.description: Returns the average percentage gain per winning trade. Calculated as the sum of profit percentages divided by the number of winning trades.

strategy.opentrades.capital_held.name: strategy.opentrades.capital_held

dayofweek.sunday.name: dayofweek.sunday
dayofweek.sunday.description: Is a named constant for return value of [dayofweek](#fun_dayofweek) function and value of [dayofweek](#var_dayofweek) variable.

strategy.oca.none.name: strategy.oca.none
strategy.oca.none.description: OCA type value for strategy\`s functions. The parameter determines that an order should not belong to any particular OCO group.

strategy.oca.cancel.name: strategy.oca.cancel
strategy.oca.cancel.description: OCA type value for strategy\`s functions. The parameter determines that an order should belong to an OCO group, where as soon as an order is filled, all other orders of the same group are cancelled. Note: if more than 1 guaranteed-to-be-executed orders of the same OCA group are placed at once, all those orders are filled.

strategy.oca.reduce.name: strategy.oca.reduce
strategy.oca.reduce.description: OCA type value for strategy\`s functions. The parameter determines that an order should belong to an OCO group, where if X number of contracts of an order is filled, number of contracts for each other order of the same OCO group is decreased by X. Note: if more than 1 guaranteed-to-be-executed orders of the same OCA group are placed at once, all those orders are filled.

strategy.commission.percent.name: strategy.commission.percent
strategy.commission.percent.description: Commission type for an order. A percentage of the cash volume of order.

strategy.commission.cash_per_contract.name: strategy.commission.cash_per_contract
strategy.commission.cash_per_contract.description: Commission type for an order. Money displayed in the account currency per contract.

strategy.commission.cash_per_order.name: strategy.commission.cash_per_order
strategy.commission.cash_per_order.description: Commission type for an order. Money displayed in the account currency per order.

strategy.fixed.name: strategy.fixed
strategy.fixed.description:
This is one of the arguments that can be supplied to the `default_qty_type` parameter in the [strategy](#fun_strategy) declaration statement.  
It is only relevant when no value is used for the ‘qty’ parameter in [strategy.entry](#fun_strategy.entry) or [strategy.order](#fun_strategy.order) function calls.  
It specifies that a number of contracts/shares/lots will be used to enter trades.

strategy.cash.name: strategy.cash
strategy.cash.description:
This is one of the arguments that can be supplied to the `default_qty_type` parameter in the [strategy](#fun_strategy) declaration statement.  
It is only relevant when no value is used for the ‘qty’ parameter in [strategy.entry](#fun_strategy.entry) or [strategy.order](#fun_strategy.order) function calls.  
It specifies that an amount of cash in the `strategy.account_currency` will be used to enter trades.

strategy.percent_of_equity.name: strategy.percent_of_equity
strategy.percent_of_equity.description:
This is one of the arguments that can be supplied to the `default_qty_type` parameter in the [strategy](#fun_strategy) declaration statement.  
It is only relevant when no value is used for the ‘qty’ parameter in [strategy.entry](#fun_strategy.entry) or [strategy.order](#fun_strategy.order) function calls.  
It specifies that a percentage (0-100) of equity will be used to enter trades.

strategy.direction.long.name: strategy.direction.long

strategy.direction.short.name: strategy.direction.short

barmerge.lookahead_off.name: barmerge.lookahead_off
barmerge.lookahead_off.description: Merge strategy for the requested data position. Requested barset is merged with current barset in the order of sorting bars by their close time. This merge strategy disables effect of getting data from "future" on calculation on history.

barmerge.lookahead_on.name: barmerge.lookahead_on
barmerge.lookahead_on.description: Merge strategy for the requested data position. Requested barset is merged with current barset in the order of sorting bars by their opening time. This merge strategy can lead to undesirable effect of getting data from "future" on calculation on history. This is unacceptable in backtesting strategies, but can be useful in indicators.

barmerge.gaps_off.name: barmerge.gaps_off
barmerge.gaps_off.description: Merge strategy for requested data. Data is merged continuously without gaps, all the gaps are filled with the previous nearest existing value.

barmerge.gaps_on.name: barmerge.gaps_on
barmerge.gaps_on.description: Merge strategy for requested data. Data is merged with possible gaps ([na](#var_na) values).

display.all.name: display.all

or.name: or
or.description: Logical OR. Applicable to boolean expressions. In Pine Script v6, uses short-circuit (lazy) evaluation: if the left-hand expression evaluates to true, the right-hand expression is skipped and not evaluated.

and.name: and
and.description: Logical AND. Applicable to boolean expressions. In Pine Script v6, uses short-circuit (lazy) evaluation: if the left-hand expression evaluates to false, the right-hand expression is skipped and not evaluated.

not.name: not
not.description: Logical negation (NOT). Applicable to boolean expressions.

if.name: if
if.description:
If statement defines what block of statements must be executed when conditions of the expression are satisfied.
To have access to and use the if statement, one should specify the version >= 2 of Pine Script™ language in the very first line of code, for example: //@version=6
The 4th version of Pine Script™ Language allows you to use “else if” syntax.
General code form:

switch.name: switch
switch.description: The switch operator transfers control to one of the several statements, depending on the values of a condition and expressions.
switch.syntaxExample:
[variable_declaration = ] switch expression
    value1 => local_block
    value2 => local_block
    …
    => default_local_block

[variable_declaration = ] switch
    boolean_expression1 => local_block
    boolean_expression2 => local_block
    …
    => default_local_block

for.name: for
for.description: The 'for' structure allows the repeated execution of a number of statements:
for.syntaxExample:
[var_declaration =] for counter = from_num to to_num [by step_num]
    statements | continue | break
    return_expression

for...in.name: for...in
for...in.description:
The `for...in` structure allows the repeated execution of a number of statements for each element in an array.  
It can be used with either one argument: `array_element`, or with two: `[index, array_element]`.  
The second form doesn't affect the functionality of the loop.  
It tracks the current iteration\`s index in the tuple\`s first variable.
for...in.syntaxExample:
[var_declaration =] for array_element in array_id
    statements | continue | break
    return_expression

[var_declaration =] for [index, array_element] in array_id
    statements | continue | break
    return_expression

while.name: while
while.description: The `while` statement allows the conditional iteration of a local code block.
while.syntaxExample:
variable_declaration = while boolean_expression
    …
    continue
    …
    break
    …
    return_expression

var.name: var
var.description:
**var** is the keyword used for assigning and one-time initializing of the variable.  
Normally, a syntax of assignment of variables, which doesn’t include the keyword var, results in the value of the variable being overwritten with every update of the data.  
Contrary to that, when assigning variables with the keyword var, they can “keep the state” despite the data updating, only changing it when conditions within if-expressions are met.

varip.name: varip
varip.description:
**varip** (var intrabar persist) is the keyword used for the assignment and one-time initialization of a variable or a field of a user-defined (type)(#op_type).  
It’s similar to the [var](#op_var) keyword, but variables and fields declared with [varip](#op_varip) retain their values between executions of the script on the same bar.

import.name: import
import.description:
Used to load an external [library](#fun_library) into a script and bind its functions to a namespace.  
The importing script can be an indicator, a strategy, or another library.  
A library must be published (privately or publicly) before it can be imported.

export.name: export
export.description: Used in libraries to prefix the declaration of functions or user-defined type definitions that will be available from other scripts importing the library.

true.name: true
true.description: Literal representing one of the values a [bool](#op_bool) variable can hold, or an expression can evaluate to when it uses comparison or logical operators.

false.name: false
false.description: Literal representing a [bool](#op_bool) value, and result of a comparison operation.

type.name: type
type.description: This keyword allows the declaration of user-defined types (UDT) from which scripts can instantiate objects. UDTs are composite types that contain an arbitrary number of fields of any built-in or user-defined type, including the defined UDT itself. The syntax to define a UDT is:

method.name: method
method.description: This keyword is used to prefix a function declaration, indicating it can then be invoked using dot notation by appending its name to a variable of the type of its first parameter and omitting that first parameter. Alternatively, functions declared as methods can also be invoked like normal user-defined functions. In that case, an argument must be supplied for its first parameter. The first parameter of a method declaration must be explicitly typified.

continue.name: continue
continue.description: The 'continue' operator, when used in a for loop, will skip the rest of the code and move to the next iteration of the loop.

break.name: break
break.description: The 'break' operator, when used in a for loop, will break out of the loop and not continue to the next iteration.

enum.name: enum
enum.description: Declares an enumeration type. Enum fields are const values of a unique type. Members are referenced as EnumName.field_name.
